sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Add explicit positive-domain constraints for loadPatchHeight and loadPatchLength by constraining their nested qudt:numericValue values with sh:minExclusive 0, and do not rely on the formula query's FILTER guards: as written, a zero or negative dimension is filtered out of the query and can pass accidentally. Retain the existing owner paths, units, selectedPeakPressureFactor comparison, same-node linkage to hasTableLookupCase, and expected-result-scaled tolerance.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the owner/path structure and datatype constraints. Remove tableReference and lookupSelectionEvidence from PeakLookupCaseShape: both properties have requiredOwner tableLookupCase and must occur only on the separately linked hasTableLookupCase node; retain only localizedStructuralMemberCategory and selectedPeakPressureFactor on the peak-pressure lookup case. Remove the guessed xsd:decimal sh:datatype constraints from every qudt:numericValue because no canonical datatype is declared. Replace the formula query's ABS usage with supported arithmetic/comparison and simple piecewise constructs, while retaining tolerance scaled from the expected result and the kN-to-MN factor 0.001.

The candidate still omits required semantic linkage and comparison for the table lookup result. Link the ship's peakPressureFactor result to the selectedPeakPressureFactor on the hasPeakPressureFactorLookupCase node, and constrain the result to the selected Table 3 value without allowing a missing branch or presence-only approximation. Also link that peak-pressure lookup case to the separately required hasTableLookupCase node so its localized category and selected factor are demonstrably selected from IACS UR I2 Table 3; do not leave the two lookup cases as disconnected mandatory nodes. The required cross-owner linkage path is absent from the supplied canonical context, so locate and use its canonical term/path.

The candidate preserves the valid owner placement, unit constraints, arithmetic tolerance, selectedPeakPressureFactor term, and separate tableLookupCase structure, but it still fails the prior required repair: hasPeakPressureFactorLookupCase is not linked to the separately required hasTableLookupCase. The SPARQL merely requires two distinct cases and a Table 3 reference, so an unrelated peak lookup case can pass accidentally. Locate the canonical cross-owner relationship/path absent from the supplied scoped vocabulary, add it to the peak lookup case structure, and constrain that linked table case to iacsUrI2Table3 with its required evidence and tableReference. Retain the prior instructions, including no guessed numeric datatype and no ABS.

Add explicit positive-domain constraints for loadPatchHeight and loadPatchLength by constraining their nested qudt:numericValue values with sh:minExclusive 0, and do not rely on the formula query's FILTER guards: as written, a zero or negative dimension is filtered out of the query and can pass accidentally. Retain the existing owner paths, units, selectedPeakPressureFactor comparison, same-node linkage to hasTableLookupCase, and expected-result-scaled tolerance.

sheets.name: VOCAB_MATCHES
rows: The candidate still omits required semantic linkage and comparison for the table lookup result. Link the ship's peakPressureFactor result to the selectedPeakPressureFactor on the hasPeakPressureFactorLookupCase node, and constrain the result to the selected Table 3 value without allowing a missing branch or presence-only approximation. Also link that peak-pressure lookup case to the separately required hasTableLookupCase node so its localized category and selected factor are demonstrably selected from IACS UR I2 Table 3; do not leave the two lookup cases as disconnected mandatory nodes. The required cross-owner linkage path is absent from the supplied canonical context, so locate and use its canonical term/path.

Use this exact term because the lookup case must link the ship's peak-pressure-factor result to the selected Table 3 factor as a unitless quantity, rather than representing only presence or an unconstrained table lookup.

The candidate preserves the valid owner placement, unit constraints, arithmetic tolerance, selectedPeakPressureFactor term, and separate tableLookupCase structure, but it still fails the prior required repair: hasPeakPressureFactorLookupCase is not linked to the separately required hasTableLookupCase. The SPARQL merely requires two distinct cases and a Table 3 reference, so an unrelated peak lookup case can pass accidentally. Locate the canonical cross-owner relationship/path absent from the supplied scoped vocabulary, add it to the peak lookup case structure, and constrain that linked table case to iacsUrI2Table3 with its required evidence and tableReference. Retain the prior instructions, including no guessed numeric datatype and no ABS.

Use this exact term because it is the canonical object property linking the peak pressure factor lookup case to the required tableLookupCase, whose tableReference can be constrained to iacsUrI2Table3 with its required evidence.
